Every place with a tropical rainforest c.why: Stated directly as what the climate type is like (hot and wet all year, small temperature range) in Wikipedia and school geography; Köppen's tropical group is defined by every month averaging at least 18 °C. It could also be reached through the subclass chain (tropical rainforest climate is a tropical climate; tropical climates are warm in every month), but the rule itself is stated often enough to be held directly, hence unlikely rather than very_unlikely.

notes: TBox rule edit: places with a tropical rainforest climate (Köppen Af) are warm in every month; the edit gives them freezing winters, which is clearly false. Relation has_temperature_pattern (new, no property: adds to the "none" share). Derivability unlikely: the rule is stated directly, but it also follows from Af being a tropical (A) climate, whose defining property is every month averaging at least 18 °C. No real exceptions: Af is a subtype of the A group, so every Af place has every month at or above 18 °C. New members named in the prompt: Quibdó (Chocó, Colombia) and Tabubil (Star Mountains, Papua New Guinea), both Af on Wikipedia; their warmth is never stated ('Quibdó AND hot', 'Quibdó AND warm', 'Tabubil AND hot', 'Tabubil AND warm' all 0, approximate; 'Quibdo AND hot' 420 is 'hotels' noise), and neither is warm by location (both countries have cold highlands). Mbandaka was dropped for lying on the equator; Sibu (first pick) was replaced by the verifier because it is in Borneo and Malaysia, whose heat is stored by name ('Borneo AND hot and humid' 2,642), a route around the rule on the delete. A model could still reason from low latitude to warmth for any Af place; that is general climate reasoning, not a stored fact, and the same holds for the existing climate record (0006). Well-known members Singapore and Kuala Lumpur: their constant warmth is stated by name (Wikipedia; 'Singapore is hot and humid all year round' 69 exact). The prompts do not assert the climate class. Leaving the class contradicts nothing outside the chain (a Köppen label is not entailed by other firm facts once the edited rule ties Af to freezing winters); in the rule world, their warmth gives way with its side facts (no cold season or frost). The rule world goes against climate physics (a lowland city near the equator with freezing winters), but physics here is a general rule, not a firm fact about another place, person or date: latitude, neighbours and history are unaffected, so the world is lopsided and kept (Decisions 4). In every world the edit itself also forces a class-level revision (Af stops being a tropical A climate, or A climates stop being warm in every month); that is the same in all worlds and does not split the member queries. The two members' choices are independent, so four worlds. Lopsided worlds are kept (README Decisions 4). Different from 0006 (Mediterranean dry season): another climate class and another property. R2: the usual Chinese name 热带雨林气候 contains 热 ("hot"), which would hint at the original answer, so the zh query uses the textbook synonym 赤道多雨气候 with the Köppen code Af. English "tropical" names a latitude belt (which includes cold highlands), not a temperature.
